items.why: I / he / she / it → was. You / we / they → were.

items.q: Today it’s hot, but yesterday it ___ cold.

items.a: I was at home last night

lines: Neil is from Liverpool. He [was|were|is] a clever child.
His parents [weren’t|wasn’t|aren’t] rich and he [wasn’t|weren’t|isn’t] at an expensive school, but he [was|were|is] happy.
Suzy is from London. Her parents [were|was|are] very rich and she [was|were|is] at an expensive school.
But she [wasn’t|weren’t|isn’t] happy, because her parents [weren’t|wasn’t|aren’t] happy together.
“[Were|Was|Are] you a happy child?” — “Yes, I [was|were|am]. There [were|was|are] six children in our family.”

tts: Suzy was at an expensive school.
She wasn’t happy as a child.

items.s: 1 — Suzy was at an expensive school.

acts.title: Where were you born?
text: “Where were you born?” — “In Malmö, in Sweden.” 👶
“Were you born in 1964?” — “No, I wasn’t. I was born in 1980.”
“Were you a happy child?” — “Yes, I was.”
“There were six children in our family. My parents weren’t rich, but we were very happy.” 😊
“Was your grandfather a doctor too?” — “No, he wasn’t. He was a shop assistant.”

write.q: Write your timeline: 5 sentences. Where you were born, where you were last year, and two things that weren’t true about your childhood.
write.model: I was born in Karaganda in 1996. I was a quiet child. My parents weren’t rich, but we were very happy. Last year I was in Almaty for my new job. Yesterday I was at home all day — it was cold and rainy.

speak.q: Answer out loud: Where were you born? Where were you yesterday? Were you a happy child?
speak.model: I was born in Karaganda. Yesterday I was at the office until six. Yes, I was — my family wasn’t rich, but we were happy.
